original_question: Let B(theta) be the Brjuno function and r(theta) the infimum of radii of convergence of linearizations for injective germs on the unit disk with multiplier e^{2 pi i theta}. Does the function log r(theta)+B(theta) extend from irrational theta to all theta in [0,1) as a 1/2-Holder continuous function?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1, in the formulation sharpened by Proposition 1.2: the Marmi–Moussa–Yoccoz conjecture that the correction term Υ(θ):=\log r(θ)+B(θ), initially defined for irrational rotation numbers, extends to all rotation numbers as a 1/2-Hölder continuous function.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the main mathematical object and the main regularity claim: it uses the Brjuno function B(θ), the Yoccoz-type linearization-radius function r(θ), restricts the initial domain to irrational θ, and asks exactly about extension to all parameters with exponent 1/2 Hölder regularity. That is the right conjectural regularity problem targeted in the paper.
missing_details: The paper packages the quantity as a single function, usually denoted Υ(θ)=\log r(θ)+B(θ); making that explicit makes the question stand alone and paper-faithful.
The parameter space is naturally modulo 1 (equivalently on \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}, or on [0,1) with 1-periodic identification), not just an arbitrary interval presentation.
The pre-extension domain should be stated precisely: irrational \theta, since B(\theta) is initially defined there and r(\theta) is used there before extension.

The definition of r(\theta) should specify that the infimum is taken over holomorphic germs f(z)=e^{2\pi i\theta}z+O(z^2) that are univalent/injective on the unit disk, and that r(\theta) is the radius of convergence of the unique formal linearization tangent to the identity.
The definition of B(\theta) should be identified as the Brjuno (Yoccoz/Brjuno) function coming from the continued-fraction expansion of \theta; otherwise the notation is not fully stand-alone.
The extension claim should say explicitly whether the target is all of \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z} or, equivalently, all of [0,1) by periodicity.

If one wants to stay maximally close to the paper, the question should not drift to neighboring quadratic-polynomial or Siegel-disk formulations unless the paper itself explicitly makes that equivalence nearby.
refined_question: Let B(\theta) be the Brjuno function, defined for irrational \theta\in\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}, and let r(\theta) be Yoccoz's radius function: the infimum, over all holomorphic germs f(z)=e^{2\pi i\theta}z+O(z^2) that are injective on the unit disk, of the radius of convergence of the unique formal linearization of f tangent to the identity. If we set \u03a5(\theta)=\log r(\theta)+B(\theta) for irrational \theta, does \u03a5 extend to a 1/2-H\u00f6lder continuous function on all of \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z} (equivalently, on [0,1) with endpoints identified)?
justification: The draft is close to the paper's intended conjecture, but it leaves implicit the paper's packaged notation \u03a5(\theta), the mod-1 parameter space, and the exact Yoccoz-style definition of r(\theta). The nearby introductory results singled out in the paper fix precisely this scope: Conjecture 1.1 is the 1/2-H\u00f6lder extension problem for \u03a5; Proposition 1.2 provides the paper's sharpened reformulation; and Theorem 1.3 gives the paper's proved regularity statement around that same function, confirming that the conjecture is about this specific correction term and not a broader linearization problem.
